questions.q: A block has width 64 and 8 heads. What does each head attend with?
options: 8 channels of its own, after the width is cut into 8
questions.answer: 8 channels of its own, after the width is cut into 8
questions.why: Heads split the width. 64 ÷ 8 = 8 channels each, joined again afterwards.

questions.q: With 24 query heads and 8 key and value heads, how many attention matrices are made?
options: 24, because each query head still makes one
questions.answer: 24, because each query head still makes one
questions.why: GQA shares keys and values, not queries. The keys repeat to line up with 24 query heads. The lab prints this rule.

questions.q: Why does a RoPE score depend only on the gap between two tokens?
options: Rotating both by their positions leaves only the difference of their angles in the dot product
The tokens are sorted before attention
Positions are divided by the image size
questions.answer: Rotating both by their positions leaves only the difference of their angles in the dot product
questions.why: Each pair's dot product depends on the angle between the two rotated vectors, and that is (n − m) × ωᵢ.

questions.q: You add an ordinary position vector to q and k. What changes compared with RoPE?
options: The score changes when you move both tokens, even with the same gap
It stops working on a CPU
questions.answer: The score changes when you move both tokens, even with the same gap
questions.why: The lab's last column shows it: same gap, different scores.

questions.q: A FLUX-type model reports an error that its axis widths don't add up. What is the likely cause?
options: The config or detection doesn't match the checkpoint
questions.answer: The config or detection doesn't match the checkpoint
questions.why: Flux raises this when sum(axes_dim) differs from its positional width, which comes from the config.
